etymologies.etymologyHTML: From fresh +‎ man.

definitions.definition: (US, Canada, Philippines) a person (of either sex) entering the first year of an institution, especially a high school (ninth grade for US, grade 9 for  Canada, grade 7 for Philippines), a university, or legislative body

quote.citation: 1596, Thomas Nashe, Have with You to Saffron-Walden:
quote.text: When he was but yet a freshman in Cambridge.

quote.citation: 1611, Thomas Middleton, The Roaring Girl, act 3, scene 3:
quote.text: Sir Alexander: Then he's a graduate.Sir Davy: Say they trust him not?Sir Alexander: Then is he held a freshman and a sot,¶ And never shall commence, but being still barr'd¶ Be expuls'd from the master's side to th' twopenny ward,¶ Or else i' th' hole be plac'd.

quote.citation: 2019 September 25, Geoffrey Kabaservice, “Impeach Trump? The United States is now in uncharted waters”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: As a country, we now enter what the seven freshmen called “unchartered waters”, with an unprecedented political and constitutional crisis looming on the horizon.

quote.citation: January 7 2023, Lisa Mascaro, Farnoush Amiri, “McCarthy elected House speaker in rowdy post-midnight vote”, in AP News‎[2]:
quote.text: Trump may have played a role in swaying some holdouts — calling into a meeting of Republican freshmen the night before, and calling other members ahead of voting.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) a novice; one in the rudiments of knowledge

quote.citation: 1619 August 6, James Howell, The Familiar Letters of James Howell, volume 1, published 1892, Letter XIII, page 39:
quote.text: I am but a Freshman yet in France, therefore I can send you no News but that all is here quiet, and 'tis no ordinary News that the French should be quiet.
